ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because the same cards serve both builds in opposite ways: Parkelj, the Robber-Knight and the Dragon drain the hoard but act as Wake triggers in the chain, and Rest doubles any other tribe's buffs, so every board makes new overlaps.
ratings_why.distinct: A doubling counter plus a 'hits zero' event is fresh, but 'don't move it' sits close to Hedgerow folk's turns-in-slot clocks.

verdict_why: The rules now read cleanly and nothing loops without a cap; more passes would change it rather than improve it.

points.text: Parkelj takes exactly the 2 Rest a Sleeper builds, so he makes each unmoved Sleeper Wake every turn, but Cloister Keeper's neighbours keep 1 and never Wake. That slot choice is great; a card that wants exactly 1 Rest left over would reward it.

The Robber-Knight's lending also empties your own units, so it is a free Start of Combat Wake round every fight. Placing it before or after the Dragon of the Springs in reading order is a real puzzle; worth calling out in the builds.
The Eldest stops gain-Wakes, but Parkelj and the Knight still empty Rest, so a hybrid hoard-and-wake board exists. Naming it as a build would show the tribe's depth.
Gift-Shop Friar only turns Rest into gold. If a sold unit passed its Rest to a neighbour instead, selling would become a combo move, not just economy.
Hanging Horseshoe Bat loses Hunker when the Dragon floods its Rest. A Wake on it (say, gain Shield) would turn that anti-synergy into a choice.

standouts.why: Parkelj the Dark is an anti-synergy that becomes the Wake engine: the best off-purpose card in the tribe.
Cowbell Kurent's Wake buffs use up the neighbours' Rest and make them Wake too, so two side by side are a real domino.
The Robber-Knight turns a buff resource into a debuff and sets off your own Wakes on the way.

weakest.why: Gift-Shop Friar does one obvious job.
Dormouse Pilgrim is plain gold for standing still, with nothing to combine.
Hanging Horseshoe Bat is a body with a conditional keyword and no other hooks.

flags.note: Mother Ribica counts fight Wakes, and the Dragon or Knight give about seven free Wakes every fight, so copies may come every turn late on.
The Eldest's permanent doubling with another tribe's share-based growth compounds; needs the runaway check.
With a hoard of 8 Rest per unit, the Robber-Knight takes 8 Attack off each enemy across, every fight.
